text:
tasha: quick one - noticed a bunch of retried requests missing our X-Request-Id header in logs, makes tracing really noisy. Seen on Kotlin SDK sample app + prod traffic mirroring.

li: how are you setting X-Request-Id today?

tasha: we were relying on a ThreadLocal MDC that our coroutine bridge populates. Interceptor reads MDC and does `request.newBuilder().header("X-Request-Id", mdc.get("reqId"))` before proceed(). Works for first attempt but retried clones sometimes lack it.

sam: that smells like a thread-context propagation issue. OkHttp retries (call.clone()/enqueue) can run on dispatcher threads which don't have the original coroutine ThreadLocal. Kotlin coroutines don't automatically propagate ThreadLocal unless you use ThreadContextElement.

li: here's the interceptor we used:
```kotlin
class TraceInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val reqId = MDC.get("reqId") // ThreadLocal sourced
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder().header("X-Request-Id", reqId ?: UUID.randomUUID().toString()).build()
    return chain.proceed(req)
  }
}
```

anya: when OkHttp retries, it may schedule the retry on a pooled thread where MDC isn't set. So header ends up null on cloned requests. Java SDK solved this by eagerly stamping headers in the calling thread before handing Call to OkHttp.

tasha: ah - so parity gap between Java & Kotlin SDKs. Java made header stamping part of the API request builder, Kotlin relied on interceptor + ThreadLocal.

sam: quick fixes: 1) stamp trace header as soon as you create the Request (i.e., at the call site before enqueue/execute) so clones inherit headers, or 2) use a CoroutineContext element that propagates MDC to threads (ThreadContextElement) and install it where coroutines are launched, or 3) change interceptor to read a header carrier from a Request.tag() (explicitly attached at creation).

li: example (stamp early):
```kotlin
val req = originalRequest.newBuilder()
  .header("X-Request-Id", currentReqId)
  .build()
service.call(req)
```
This guarantees call.clone() will carry the header.

anya: for SDK sample app we should prefer an explicit approach so users don't accidentally rely on ThreadLocal. Also doc the coroutine-to-ThreadLocal pitfalls.

tasha: I pushed a branch: stamp header at request creation in sample, and added a utility `Tracing.tag(request, reqId)` which stores it in Request.tag for interceptor fallback. Also added integration test that simulates a 401-triggered retry and asserts X-Request-Id appears on all server-side records.

sam: please also add a short note in the SDK "Auth & Retry" doc: "Do not rely on ThreadLocal MDC for request-scoped headers when using coroutines + OkHttp; prefer explicit header stamping or coroutine ThreadContextElement." Include the sample snippet and guidance for Java/Kotlin parity.

devops-bot: mirror deployed: sample/trace-fix branch validated in staging replay for 2k requests, no header loss observed.

li: one more gotcha: if you stamp header lazily in an interceptor but also refresh auth (which may mutate header) you must ensure auth refresh updates the stamped header before retries. Prefer a single place to stamp final headers (call site) or a deterministic two-step: stamp tracing first, then auth header in network interceptor that runs per-request and can be updated safely.

tasha: added that note in README and a short runbook entry for on-call: "Missing X-Request-Id on retried requests -> check if trace stamping used ThreadLocal; if so, validate sample app or switch to request-stamped headers." PR opened #5273 with tests and docs. Thanks all :coffee:
